name: Chris Wanstrath
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded GitHub and publicly launched it in April 2008 at age 23; the platform reached 100,000 users by July 2009 and became the world's largest code host.
early_history_summary: Wanstrath grew up in Cincinnati, Ohio, and taught himself programming as a teenager to make video games. He briefly studied English at the University of Cincinnati before dropping out in 2005 to move to San Francisco and work at CNET on GameSpot and Chowhound. He ran a Ruby on Rails consulting shop with PJ Hyett before co-founding GitHub in 2008.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Cincinnati, Ohio; parents not described in detail in reviewed sources. He was self-taught as a programmer from a young age, making games and websites as a teen.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental tech or entrepreneurial background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught programmer, SF tech ecosystem, complementary co-founders, Git/open-source wave, developer domain proximity
evidence_summary: Wanstrath was a self-taught programmer from Cincinnati who dropped out of college to move to San Francisco for a CNET job in 2005. He built Ruby on Rails expertise through consulting with PJ Hyett before co-founding GitHub in 2008 at age 23. No family tech background or financial safety net is documented; his advantages were self-created through relentless coding practice, moving to the SF tech frontier, and teaming with strong co-founders. GitHub rode the wave of Git adoption and open-source collaboration to become the world's largest code host.
starting_point: Born in 1985 in Cincinnati, Ohio; grew up in a middle-class family with no documented tech or entrepreneurial background; self-taught programming as a teenager.
current_position: Founder of Null Games; former GitHub CEO and Microsoft Technical Fellow; net worth estimated at $1.8-2.2 billion; resides in San Francisco.

trajectory.event: Dropped out of University of Cincinnati and moved to San Francisco to work as a web developer at CNET on GameSpot and other sites.
Co-founded GitHub with Tom Preston-Werner and PJ Hyett; public launch in April 2008, reaching 100,000 users within a year.
GitHub raised Series A funding from Andreessen Horowitz at a valuation reportedly around $750 million.
Microsoft acquired GitHub for $7.5 billion in an all-stock deal; Wanstrath became a billionaire as the largest individual shareholder.
Founded Null Games, an independent game publishing studio, after leaving Microsoft.

name: Blake Ross
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created the Firefox web browser (originally Phoenix) with Dave Hyatt, first released in September 2002 at age 17; Firefox 1.0 launched November 9, 2004 at age 19 and was downloaded 27 million+ times, challenging Internet Explorer's dominance.
early_history_summary: Ross grew up in Key Biscayne, Florida, with his mother (a psychologist) and father (a lawyer). He created his first website at age 10 and started fixing bugs for the Mozilla project at age 14, which led to a summer internship at Netscape in Mountain View in 2001. He co-created Firefox (then called Phoenix) with Dave Hyatt in 2002 while still in high school, and Firefox 1.0 launched in November 2004 when he was a 19-year-old Stanford sophomore.
family_context_summary: Raised in Key Biscayne, Florida; mother Abby Ross is a psychologist, father David Ross is a lawyer. Parents fostered his interest in computers, with his mother driving him across the country for his Netscape internship. He attended Gulliver Preparatory School.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Mozilla open-source community, early coding, Netscape internship, complementary co-creator, browser wars wave, professional parents
evidence_summary: Ross was coding from age 10 and contributing to the Mozilla project by 14, leveraging the open-source community as both a learning platform and distribution channel. His parents, a psychologist and lawyer, supported his interest and facilitated his Netscape internship at 14. He co-created Firefox with Dave Hyatt at 17 and launched Firefox 1.0 at 19, achieving 27M+ downloads and challenging Internet Explorer. His deep early immersion in the Mozilla codebase and the open-source browser movement were the primary drivers of his precocious success.
starting_point: Born in 1985 in Miami, Florida; raised in Key Biscayne by a psychologist mother and lawyer father who supported his early computing interests; attended Gulliver Preparatory School.
current_position: Independent; former Director of Product at Facebook (2007-2013); estimated net worth ~$150 million; resides in New York City.

trajectory.event: Co-created Phoenix (later Firefox) with Dave Hyatt; first public release Phoenix 0.1 on September 23, 2002.
Firefox 1.0 launched on November 9, 2004; downloaded 27 million+ times, challenging Internet Explorer's browser dominance.

Co-founded Parakey, a web OS startup, with Joe Hewitt.
Parakey acquired by Facebook as its first acquisition; Ross joined Facebook as an engineer.
Left Facebook as Director of Product after six years to pursue new projects.
Purchased an $8.25 million condominium in Soho, New York City.

name: Håkon Wium Lie

name: Jon Bosak
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. At age 26 (1974) he was early in his career. He led the creation of XML at W3C in 1996-1998 at age 48-50, and worked at Sun Microsystems from 1996 to 2008.
early_history_summary: Bosak organized and led the W3C technical committee that created XML, which became a W3C Recommendation in 1998. He was named 'Father of XML' by the W3C in 2000. Before XML, he managed Novell's online documentation repository using SGML (1990-1994) and worked at Sun Microsystems as a Distinguished Engineer (2000-2008). His father, Robert Bosak, was a computer industry pioneer who worked on the first computer on the west coast of the US in 1947 and joined RAND in 1948.
